fix:
Newly inserted nodes clone every label, value, description, state and action list here, and then the drain loop in the same function moves the same values again through semantics.update. The comment at lines 453-454 claims one copy only, but this loop makes a second one. Insert a placeholder with the empty value of each field, since the drain loop writes all content right after:
let id = self.semantics.insert(SemanticNode {
    id: SemanticNodeId(ArenaId::from_parts(0, 0)),
    role: build.role,
    label: Default::default(),
    value: Default::default(),
    description: Default::default(),
    bounds: build.bounds,
    state: Default::default(),
    actions: Default::default(),
    children: Vec::new(),
});
(Use the empty value of each field type if one of them has no Default impl. Check that the devtools revision comparison below is unaffected: it is taken after this insert, so it is.)

Every fully rebuilt node allocates a fresh children Vec from the reusable child_ids scratch. The Bounds arm at line 495 already passes child_ids as a slice to update_geometry. Give the full-update path the same slice-based write (in the semantics graph module) so the existing node's children Vec is overwritten in place and keeps its capacity, then drop the clone here. Verify first that update_geometry copies into the existing Vec and does not replace it.

This linear scan runs for every child of every SliverViewport visited in a pass, so a viewport with N visited children costs O(N^2). The same scan is repeated at line 658 in collect_semantics_inner. Have the parent supply the slot: add a slot: u32 field to SemanticVisit, filled while the parent enumerates its children, and use it here and at line 658 instead of position(). Keep position() only as a fallback where no slot is available.

Turn the allow into an expect that carries its reason, and drop the separate comment:
#[expect(clippy::large_enum_variant, reason = "Boxing the full build would add an allocation per rebuilt node.")]
Run cargo clippy afterwards to confirm the lint still fires, since expect fails when it does not.

Parent is encoded as a u32 with two sentinel values, both of which are read back by comparison (for example edges[cursor].0 == index as u32 at line 459 and parent != RETAINED_LIST at line 216). Replace them with an enum carried by SemanticVisit::parent and the edges tuple:
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum SemanticParent { TopLevel, RetainedList, Build(u32) }
Note that the edge tuple grows from 4 to 8 bytes, so measure the effect on the semantics pass before adopting it.
